thread:
ops-bot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx/error-rate spike: model-runner-prod-eu (all AZs). Err rate 0.2% -> ~9% over 5m. Symptoms: 502/503, timeouts, occasional segfaults. See alert: https://internal/alerts/1847004321

matt_oncall: i'm paged, looking. which model/route is spiking? any obvious rollout?

jen_sre: quick grep of logs shows repeated OOMs then SIGSEGV in model_runner_3 pod on node gpu-eu-12. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-14T12:07:03Z] model_runner_3[pid:4231]: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-14T12:07:05Z] model_runner_3[pid:4231]: terminating with signal SIGSEGV
[2026-03-14T12:07:05Z] model_runner_3: stack trace: at attention_kernel_init+0x1f3
```

kai_runtime: confirm — reproducer with long seq (3k tokens) pushes VRAM then kernel crashes. Looks like a regression in the attention kernel that surfaced under larger batch/seq length.

matt_oncall: initial mitigations? can we drop batching or reduce max_seq for the route? any quick hotfix?

kai_runtime: yes. proposed immediate mitigations:
- disable dynamic batching for model-x-prod
- short-circuit requests over 2048 tokens with 429 or reroute to legacy model variant
- spin up extra gpu nodes and shorten restart backoff to replace bad pods quickly
- route a small % (20%) to quantized fallback model-x-prod-q4 while we triage

jen_sre: applying changes now. commands:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/model-runner ENABLE_DYNAMIC_BATCHING=false --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-runner
```

deploy-bot: rollout restart started for deploy/model-runner (rev 2026-03-14-42). Watch: https://k8s.internal/rollouts/../2026

customer-ops: alerting top impacted customers: acme-inc, pixly, ledgerly. Drafting status page: "Investigating elevated inference errors; mitigation in progress."

jen_sre: after disable+restart: error rate dropped from ~9% -> ~3.4% within 3 minutes. A few pods (gpu-eu-12, gpu-eu-15) still show elevated GPU memory and repeated coredumps. I'm killing those and letting autoscaler replace.

kai_runtime: starting canary rollback to previous stable model revision (v1.8) on 2 pods to validate stability/quality. command: `redwoodctl deploy model-x --version=v1.8 --selector=canary`

jen_sre: collecting artifacts: heap profiles, dmesg, coredumps. If coredumps present, uploading to S3 bucket for postmortem: `aws s3 cp /tmp/coredump.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-1847004321/`

ops-bot: INCIDENT created INC-2026-1847004321; severity P1 — runbook: https://goto/runbooks/model-runner-oom; pager duty on-call: matt_oncall.

matt_oncall: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml-research for kernel investigation (possible attention kernel regression). jen, kai — please coordinate. I'll stay on until handoff.

customer-ops: posted status update to status.redwood.io: "We are experiencing elevated inference error rates in EU/US. Mitigations deployed; some customers affected. No data exfiltration. Updates every 30 minutes."

kai_runtime: taking lead for the investigation. Current action items I own:
- validate crash signatures across all pods, collect versions and compile flags
- reproduce locally with long-seq workload under v1.9 runner build
- if reproduces, hotfix attention init or rollback globally to v1.8
- finalize canary results in 30m

jen_sre: note on customer impact: ~14% of requests in EU were returning 5xx at peak, US ~6%. Three enterprise customers showing >25% errors for their traffic slices. No requests show data corruption — these are inference-time failures.

matt_oncall: good. handoff plan: I'll hand primary to kai_runtime at 1847004500 (25m from now). I'll remain available for escalation for another hour. Kai, please post interim RCA and timeline after you have canary results.

kai_runtime: acknowledged. moving conversation to #eng-runtime for deeper debugging and kernel bisect. Will post updates + full timeline to incident doc INC-2026-1847004321. :thumbsup:

jen_sre: added link to logs and profiles: https://internal/logs/INC-2026-1847004321 and uploaded coredumps to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-1847004321/crash.tgz

customer-ops: sent targeted messages to affected account admins (acme-inc, pixly, ledgerly). They acknowledged; acme asked for ETA for full resolution. I told them we expect stabilization within 1 hour and a full RCA afterward.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy (model-x v1.8) shows 0 crashes on canary pods after 12m and stable memory usage.

kai_runtime: early conclusion — immediate mitigations (disable batching + fallback variant + canary rollback) restored majority of traffic. Next: kernel bisect and fix in attention_init; will coordinate with eng-ml-research. Preparing postmortem draft.

matt_oncall: handing off now. Thanks everyone for quick responses. Leaving notes in the incident doc and assigning follow-ups.

(incident doc: https://incidents/internal/INC-2026-1847004321 contains timeline, exec summary, runbook references, and links to artifacts.)
